chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Karim, the cousin of Abu Zar'a, narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn Ibrahim al-Balkhi narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, from Sadaqa ibn Yasir, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said:

This Surah, 'When comes the Help of Allah and the Victory,' was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during the middle days of al-Tashriq, so he knew that this was the Farewell Pilgrimage. He mounted his camel, al-Adha', praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: O people! Every bloodshed from the Age of Ignorance is void (hadr). The first blood to be voided is the blood of al-Harith ibn Rabi'a ibn al-Harith, who was wet-nursed among the Hudhayl and was killed by the Banu Layth, or he said: he was wet-nursed among Banu Layth and was killed by Hudhayl. And every usury from the Age of Ignorance is abolished, and the first usury to be abolished is the usury of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib.

O people! Indeed, time has revolved, and today it is as it was on the day the heavens and the earth were created. Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah on the day He created the heavens and the earth, among them four are sacred: Rajab of Mudar, which is between Jumada and Shaban, Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and al-Muharram. So do not oppress yourselves in them, for the Nasī' (delaying of sacred months) is an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it permissible one year and forbidden another, to match the number of months Allah had made sacred. They used to forbid al-Muharram one year and make Safar permissible, and forbid Safar one year and make al-Muharram permissible.
O people! Indeed, Satan has become despairing of being worshipped in your lands for the rest of eternity, so He is pleased with you for the minor deeds.
O people! Whoever has a trust/deposit with him, let him return it to the one who entrusted it to him.

O people! Indeed, women are your captives, who possess no power over themselves for harm or benefit. You have taken them in the trust of Allah and made lawful their private parts by the word of Allah. You have rights over them, and they have rights over you. Among your rights over them is that they do not let others sleep on your beds, nor disobey you in good matters. If they do so, then their provision and clothing are due to them in a fair manner, and do not beat them.
O people! I have left among you that if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty. So hold fast to it.

O people! What day is this? They said: A sacred day. Then he said: O people! What month is this? They said: A sacred month. He said: O people! What town is this? They said: A sacred town. He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, has made your blood, your wealth, and your honor forbidden among you, like the sanctity of this day of yours in this month of yours in this town of yours, until the day you meet Him. So let the present among you convey to the absent. There will be no Prophet after me and no nation after you.
Then he raised his hands until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen, then said: O Allah, bear witness that I have conveyed (the message).
ai.seo_question: What were the key legal and social rulings delivered in the Prophet's Farewell Sermon?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal records the Prophet’s Farewell Sermon, delivered on the 8th of Dhu al-Qi'dah (or 7th, depending on interpretation of 'middle of Tashriq' contextually linked to the revelation of Surah al-Nasr), marking the culmination of his mission. It establishes foundational Shia and Sunni legal principles, including the abrogation of Jahiliyyah customs like blood feuds and usury, the sanctity of time and space, and the reciprocal rights of spouses, while affirming the Qur'an as the enduring safeguard against misguidance.
